en: Points of Controversy The Chapter on Refutation The Eighteenth Section
Regarding the discourse on the world of humans:
Should it not be said that "the Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the world of humans"?
“Yes.
“But surely there are shrines where Buddhas have dwelt, as well as monasteries, villages, market towns, cities, kingdoms, and provinces?
“Yes.”
If there are indeed shrines established by the Buddha, as well as monasteries, villages, market towns, cities, kingdoms, and provinces, then indeed, sir, it should be said:
"The Blessed Buddha dwelt in the world of men.
It should not be said [that he did not].
“Did the Buddha, the Blessed One, dwell in the world of humans?”— “Yes.”—

“But was it not the case that the Blessed One was born at Lumbinī, attained full enlightenment at the foot of the Bodhi tree, set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion by the Blessed One at Bārāṇasī, relinquished the life-force at the Cāpāla Shrine, and the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna at Kusinārā?”
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If the Blessed One was born at Lumbinī … and the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna at Kusinārā, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
‘The Buddha, the Blessed One, remained in the world of men.’”
Is it not to be said that the Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the world of men?
Yes, it is.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
"Bhikkhus, on one occasion I was dwelling at Ukkaṭṭhā in the Subhaga Grove at the foot of a king-sāla tree"; and:
"Bhikkhus, on one occasion, having just attained full enlightenment, I was dwelling at Uruvelā at the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree"?
“Bhikkhus, on one occasion I was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place”;
“Bhikkhus, on one occasion I was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park”;
“Bhikkhus, on one occasion I was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.”
Is this indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, the Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the world of humans.
“Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, dwell in the world of human beings?”— “Yes.”—
“But was the Blessed One not born in the world, raised in the world, and yet dwells having overcome the world, unsullied by the world?”
“Yes.
“If it is true that the Blessed One was born in the world, grew up in the world, and dwells having overcome the world, unsullied by the world, then surely it should not be said:
‘The Buddha, the Blessed One, stood in the human world.’”
The Discussion on the World of Human Beings is finished.
